title: WebSocket Real-Time Connections
content:
Gravito's **BunNativeAdapter** provides native WebSocket support at the adapter layer. Register routes with customized handlers for open, message, close, and drain events.

Basic WebSocket Setup

Register a WebSocket route with BunNativeAdapter:

import { PlanetCore, defineConfig } from '@gravito/core'
import { BunNativeAdapter } from '@gravito/core'

const config = defineConfig({
  adapter: new BunNativeAdapter(),
  config: { PORT: 3000 }
})

async function main() {
  const core = await PlanetCore.boot(config)
  const adapter = core.adapter as BunNativeAdapter
  
  // Register WebSocket route
  adapter.registerWebSocketRoute('/chat', {
    open: (ws) => {
      console.log('Client connected')
      ws.send('Welcome to chat!')
    },
    
    message: (ws, data) => {
      console.log('Message received:', data)
      // Echo back to client
      ws.send(`Echo: ${data}`)
    },
    
    close: (ws, code, reason) => {
      console.log(`Client disconnected: ${code} ${reason}`)
    }
  })
  
  // Also support regular HTTP routes
  core.router.get('/', (c) => {
    return c.html(`
      
WebSocket Chat

      

      
      
      
      
    `)
  })
  
  const liftoff = core.liftoff()
  Bun.serve(liftoff)
}

main().catch(console.error)

Wildcard Path Routing

WebSocket routes support wildcard patterns for flexible routing:

// Exact path
adapter.registerWebSocketRoute('/chat', { /* handlers */ })

// Wildcard: matches /api/ws, /api/ws-notify, etc.
adapter.registerWebSocketRoute('/api/*', {
  open: (ws) => {
    console.log('API WebSocket opened')
  },
  message: (ws, data) => {
    // Route based on parsed data or path
    console.log('API message:', data)
  }
})

Multiple Event Types

Handle all WebSocket lifecycle events:

adapter.registerWebSocketRoute('/notifications', {
  // Called when client connects
  open: (ws) => {
    console.log('Client connected')
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({
      type: 'connected',
      timestamp: Date.now()
    }))
  },
  
  // Called for each message
  message: (ws, data) => {
    // data can be string, Buffer, or Uint8Array
    if (typeof data === 'string') {
      const message = JSON.parse(data)
      console.log('User message:', message)
      
      // Send response
      ws.send(JSON.stringify({
        type: 'ack',
        id: message.id,
        received: true
      }))
    }
  },
  
  // Called when client closes connection
  close: (ws, code, reason) => {
    console.log(`Disconnected - Code: ${code}, Reason: ${reason}`)
  },
  
  // Called when ready for backpressured messages
  drain: (ws) => {
    console.log('Ready to send buffered data')
  }
})

Broadcasting to Multiple Clients

Store WebSocket connections and broadcast messages:

// Store active connections
const chatClients = new Set()

adapter.registerWebSocketRoute('/chat', {
  open: (ws) => {
    chatClients.add(ws)
    
    // Notify others
    broadcast({
      type: 'user_joined',
      count: chatClients.size
    })
  },
  
  message: (ws, data) => {
    const message = {
      type: 'chat',
      text: data.toString(),
      timestamp: Date.now()
    }
    
    // Broadcast to all clients
    broadcast(message)
  },
  
  close: (ws) => {
    chatClients.delete(ws)
    broadcast({
      type: 'user_left',
      count: chatClients.size
    })
  }
})

function broadcast(message: any) {
  const data = JSON.stringify(message)
  for (const ws of chatClients) {
    ws.send(data)
  }
}

Binary Data Handling

WebSocket supports string, Buffer, and Uint8Array data types:

adapter.registerWebSocketRoute('/data', {
  message: (ws, data) => {
    // Handle different data types
    if (typeof data === 'string') {
      console.log('String:', data)
    } else if (data instanceof Buffer) {
      console.log('Buffer:', data.length, 'bytes')
      // Send binary response
      const response = new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3, 4])
      ws.send(response)
    } else if (data instanceof Uint8Array) {
      console.log('Uint8Array:', data.length, 'bytes')
      // Send buffer response
      ws.send(Buffer.from(data).toString('hex'))
    }
  }
})

Error Handling

Defensive Programming

Always validate WebSocket state and handle errors gracefully.

adapter.registerWebSocketRoute('/secure', {
  open: (ws) => {
    try {
      // Initialize connection state
      ws.user_id = null
      console.log('Connection initialized')
    } catch (err) {
      console.error('Open handler error:', err)
      ws.close(1011, 'Internal error')
    }
  },
  
  message: async (ws, data) => {
    try {
      if (!data) {
        ws.send(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Empty message' }))
        return
      }
      
      const message = JSON.parse(data.toString())
      
      // Validate message structure
      if (!message.type) {
        ws.send(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Missing type field' }))
        return
      }
      
      // Handle different message types
      switch (message.type) {
        case 'auth':
          ws.user_id = message.user_id
          ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'auth_success' }))
          break
        
        case 'ping':
          ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'pong' }))
          break
        
        default:
          ws.send(JSON.stringify({
            error: 'Unknown message type: ' + message.type
          }))
      }
    } catch (err) {
      console.error('Message handler error:', err)
      ws.send(JSON.stringify({
        error: 'Failed to process message'
      }))
    }
  },
  
  close: (ws) => {
    try {
      console.log('Client disconnected:', ws.user_id)
    } catch (err) {
      console.error('Close handler error:', err)
    }
  }
})

Rate Limiting & Backpressure

Handle backpressure to avoid overwhelming clients:

const messageQueues = new Map()

adapter.registerWebSocketRoute('/stream', {
  open: (ws) => {
    messageQueues.set(ws, [])
  },
  
  message: (ws, data) => {
    // Check if client can accept more data
    if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
      try {
        ws.send(data)
      } catch (err) {
        // Queue message if backpressured
        messageQueues.get(ws)?.push(data)
      }
    }
  },
  
  drain: (ws) => {
    // Client is ready for more data
    const queue = messageQueues.get(ws)
    if (queue && queue.length > 0) {
      console.log(`Draining ${queue.length} queued messages`)
      while (queue.length > 0) {
        const msg = queue.shift()
        try {
          ws.send(msg)
        } catch (err) {
          queue.unshift(msg) // Re-queue on error
          break
        }
      }
    }
  },
  
  close: (ws) => {
    messageQueues.delete(ws)
  }
})

Real-World Example: Live Notifications

import { PlanetCore, defineConfig } from '@gravito/core'
import { BunNativeAdapter } from '@gravito/core'

// Store active notification connections
const notificationClients = new Map()

const config = defineConfig({
  adapter: new BunNativeAdapter(),
  config: { PORT: 3000 }
})

async function main() {
  const core = await PlanetCore.boot(config)
  const adapter = core.adapter as BunNativeAdapter
  
  // WebSocket endpoint for notifications
  adapter.registerWebSocketRoute('/notifications/:user_id', {
    open: (ws) => {
      const userId = (ws as any).data?.path?.split('/').pop()
      if (userId) {
        notificationClients.set(userId, ws)
        console.log(`User ${userId} connected`)
        ws.send(JSON.stringify({
          type: 'ready',
          message: 'Connected to notifications'
        }))
      }
    },
    
    message: (ws, data) => {
      // Client-side ping/pong
      if (data.toString() === 'ping') {
        ws.send('pong')
      }
    },
    
    close: (ws) => {
      for (const [userId, client] of notificationClients) {
        if (client === ws) {
          notificationClients.delete(userId)
          console.log(`User ${userId} disconnected`)
        }
      }
    }
  })
  
  // HTTP API to send notifications
  core.router.post('/api/notify/:user_id', async (c) => {
    const userId = c.req.param('user_id')
    const body = await c.req.json()
    
    const ws = notificationClients.get(userId)
    if (ws) {
      ws.send(JSON.stringify({
        type: 'notification',
        title: body.title,
        message: body.message,
        timestamp: Date.now()
      }))
      return c.json({ success: true })
    }
    
    return c.json({ error: 'User not connected' }, 404)
  })
  
  // Broadcast to all connected users
  core.router.post('/api/broadcast', async (c) => {
    const body = await c.req.json()
    const notification = JSON.stringify({
      type: 'broadcast',
      title: body.title,
      message: body.message,
      timestamp: Date.now()
    })
    
    let count = 0
    for (const ws of notificationClients.values()) {
      try {
        ws.send(notification)
        count++
      } catch (err) {
        console.error('Failed to send to client:', err)
      }
    }
    
    return c.json({ 
      success: true,
      notified: count,
      total: notificationClients.size
    })
  })
  
  const liftoff = core.liftoff()
  Bun.serve(liftoff)
  console.log(`🚀 Server with WebSocket running at http://localhost:3000`)
}

main().catch(console.error)

Best Practices

  • ✓
    Validate PathsAlways validate and extract path parameters before storing connections
  • ✓
    Handle Errors GracefullyUse try-catch in handlers and validate message formats
  • ✓
    Manage ConnectionsClean up connections on close to prevent memory leaks
  • ✓
    Handle BackpressureUse the drain event to handle buffered messages when client is ready
  • ✓
    Support Multiple Data TypesHandle string, Buffer, and Uint8Array for flexible message formats

Performance: WebSocket connections in BunNativeAdapter leverage Bun's native C++ implementation, delivering ultra-low latency and high throughput. The HTTP-to-WebSocket upgrade happens at the adapter layer with minimal overhead, supporting thousands of concurrent connections efficiently.
